tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.

  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.

    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)

  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).

    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:

    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.

    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

# Memo: tariff protection in the automobile sector

The question is whether the protection given to local assembly has fallen, and whether output
responded. Three things have to be pinned down: the nominal tariff on built-up imports, the tariff
on knocked-down kits, and local production.

## Tariffs

The duty on completely built-up units is reported at the Pakistan Economic Survey 2022-23 (p. 37 of the file, printed page 2-10), Table 2.3: CBU tariff rate. The
knocked-down kit rate is at the Pakistan Economic Survey 2022-23 (p. 37 of the file, printed page 2-10), Table 2.1: CKD tariff rate. The gap between the two is the
crude measure of effective protection for assembly, and it has narrowed over the window, but not
monotonically — there are two years where the built-up rate falls and the kit rate does not.

The statutory changes themselves are in the notifications rather than the survey. The relevant
ones for the window are indexed in the notifications folder; the survey table is a summary and does
not record the mid-year changes, so a year in which the rate changed in March will show the
post-change rate in the survey and the pre-change rate in anything extracted from the earlier
budget documents.

## Output

Production of cars and light commercial vehicles is at
the Pakistan Economic Survey 2022-23 (p. 38 of the file, printed page 2-11), Table 2.8: Car and LCV assembly. Note the units: thousands of vehicles, not vehicles.
An earlier draft of the chart had this wrong by three orders of magnitude and it survived two
readings before anyone noticed.

The collapse in the middle of the window is an import-compression story, not a tariff story. The
kit rate did not move in that year. The binding constraint was the letter-of-credit restriction,
which does not appear as a rate anywhere and has to be dated from the circulars.

## Revenue

If anyone asks what the tariff changes cost in revenue, the customs head is at
the White Paper on the Budget 2025-26 - Government of Balochistan (p. 110 of the file, printed page 4-13), Table 4.2: Customs receipts, but that is the whole customs take and the automobile share of it
is not separable from any document we hold. Do not let this become a number in a draft.

# Working notes for automated sessions

## Where things are

- Source PDFs: `02_sources/` — read only, never write here
- Extracted tables: `03_extraction/output/`
- Cleaned analysis-ready data: `03_extraction/clean/`
- Figures and final tables: `05_outputs/`

## Conventions

- Fiscal years are written `2019-20`, never `FY2020` or `2019/20`.
- Values are Rs billion unless the column name ends in `_mn` or `_usd`.
- Every derived table carries `source_doc` and `source_page`.

## Things that will trip you up

- Two of the provincial white papers report the development programme in Rs million while every
  other document in the same folder uses Rs billion. The conversion happens in the cleaning
  script, not in the extraction step, so the intermediate files look wrong and are not.
- The survey statistical appendix reprints earlier years with revisions. If a number does not
  match an earlier document, check the publication year before assuming an extraction error.

## Do not

- Do not rewrite files under `02_sources/`.
- Do not commit anything larger than 20 MB.
- Do not change column names in `03_extraction/clean/` without updating the codebook in the
  same commit.

# Zain's handoff — Aug 2022

I am writing this on my last week so it is probably not complete. Sorry in advance for anything I
have forgotten.

## What I was actually working on

The provincial receipts extraction. Punjab and Sindh are finished and checked. KP is extracted but
not checked — I got through about half the years before I ran out of time, and the ones I did check
were fine, so my guess is the rest are fine too, but that is a guess.

- The white papers for Punjab change their table layout in FY2016-17. Before that year the
  receipts table has the heads in the first column and the years across the top. After that year
  it is transposed. The extraction script handles both but it decides which layout it is looking
  at by counting columns, which is fragile. If a year comes out with nonsense values that is the
  first thing to check.
- Two of the Sindh documents are scans with no text underneath. I typed those tables in by hand.
  They are in `ADP execution/` and there is a note in each file saying which document and page it came
  from. Please do not lose those, retyping them took a full day.

  crosswalk in `notes/label_crosswalk.csv` but it only covers the years I got to.

## What I would do next

Finish checking KP, then do Balochistan, then decide what to do about AJK and GB. Honestly I think
AJK and GB should be handled separately because their budget documents are structured differently
enough that the same script will not work.

## Where things are

Everything is under this folder except the raw PDFs, which are in the shared sources folder. My
scratch work is in `submission/` and can be deleted, there is nothing in there that matters.

# Codebook — household survey extract

One row per household. Five rounds pooled. Weights are round-specific and must be used for any
population statement.

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `hhid` | string | Household identifier. Unique within a round, not across rounds. |
| `round` | integer | Survey round. Use with `hhid` for a unique key. |
| `province` | string | Province name as printed in the source, not a code. |
| `district` | string | District name, harmonised to the latest boundaries via the crosswalk. |
| `district_orig` | string | District name exactly as it appeared in the source file. |
| `urban` | 0/1 | 1 if urban. Definition follows the source; it changed once, see below. |
| `hhsize` | integer | Household size, all members. |
| `cons_month_hh` | float | Monthly household consumption, current rupees. Not per capita. |
| `cons_month_pc` | float | `cons_month_hh` divided by `hhsize`. |
| `food_share` | float | Food consumption as a share of `cons_month_hh`. |
| `weight` | float | Household weight for the round. |

## Notes that matter

- The urban definition changes in the third round. Before it, urban follows the administrative
  classification; after it, it follows the settlement-size rule. Anything that pools rounds and
  splits on `urban` needs to say which definition it is using or restrict to comparable rounds.
- `cons_month_hh` is nominal. There is no deflator in this file. The deflator question is still
  open and should not be resolved silently inside an analysis script.
- Missing values are blank, not a sentinel. If you see a zero in `cons_month_hh` it is a real zero
  in the source and should be treated as an error in the source, of which there are eleven.

Short answer: probably neither is "wrong" — they look like two different publication vintages, and I could not verify the document side because PDF text extraction is blocked in this session.

## What the spreadsheet says

`RA Work/auto_sector_protection/clean/auto_production_long.csv:8`

```
auto_production_units,Automobile production,2016-17,238.8,thousand units,auto_production_units::v2,F,economic_survey_2026
```

## Why it won't match the published document

The two sides are not extractions of the same document:

- The memo (`RA Work/auto_sector_protection/notes/MEMO_auto_sector_protection.md:22`) says production comes from **Economic Survey 2022-23**, Table 2.8, printed page 2-11.
- The CSV is stamped `economic_survey_2026`. By this corpus's naming convention (publication year, not fiscal year — cf. `economic_survey_2022` on the 2021-22 survey in `RA Work/tax_effort/clean/psdp_federal_series.csv`), that is **Economic Survey 2025-26**. Four years later.

And `agent_workspace/CLAUDE.md:21` states the rule directly: *"The survey statistical appendix reprints earlier years with revisions. If a number does not match an earlier document, check the publication year before assuming an extraction error."*

So 238.8 is a **latest-vintage restatement** of 2016-17; the printed survey figure is the **contemporaneous** one. The project's stated method (HEC NRPU 2019 proposal; `RA Work/tax_effort/PLAN.md`) is to record the vintage on every observation "rather than by choosing a single figure" — which makes "which is right" the wrong question by design. For a level series you want the vintage that matches your other regressors; for a single citation you want whatever the paper's text claims to cite.

## Two things to rule out first

1. **Units.** The memo flags this explicitly: thousands of vehicles, not vehicles — an earlier chart was out by three orders of magnitude and survived two readings. If the gap is ~1000×, it's this, not a revision.
2. **Which physical file the document number came from.** The corpus has many PDFs suffixed `- perturbed values` (including `Pakistan Economic Survey 2016-17 - perturbed values.pdf` in `archive/` and `Downloads/reports/world bank/`). Those contain altered figures. The citable copies are the unsuffixed ones under `Sources/Federal/Economic Survey/<year>/`. This isn't documented in any README — I've saved it to memory.

## What I couldn't do

I could not open Table 2.8 to give you the published figure. `pdftotext` exists at `/mingw64/bin/pdftotext` but every invocation was denied, and the Read tool needs `pdftoppm`, which isn't installed. If you approve `pdftotext` (or install poppler), the check is one command against `Sources/Federal/Economic Survey/2022-23/`, p. 38.

One more gap worth knowing: `vintage_label` is `::v2`, but no v1 is retained anywhere — `clean/superseded/` is empty and the series appears in only one file in the whole corpus. The earlier vintage that would reconcile against the 2022-23 survey isn't stored, so it has to be re-extracted rather than looked up.
